decisions.rationale: Talonflame leads with Gale Wings +1 priority Tailwind for speed control. Spiritomb walls Mega Gengar (Shadow Ball 31-54%, Sludge Bomb 17-29%) and threatens Sucker Punch. Rotom-Wash in back guarantees Gyarados OHKO with Thunderbolt and walls Mamoswine (immune EQ, Ice Shard only 8-13%). Floette is the Tailwind sweeper—Psychic hits Gengar/Toxapex, Moonblast covers Gyarados. This 4 covers all six of their threats.

Rotom-Wash Thunderbolt guarantees Gyarados OHKO (103-228%) and walls Mamoswine (Levitate immune EQ, resists Ice Shard 8-13%). Floette Psychic vs Gengar 57-136% (not guaranteed OHKO on bulkier sets). Toxapex very bulky—need repeated Psychics or EQ. If game 2: consider Garchomp if they drop Mamoswine, Aegislash if spread spam is problematic.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados+Mamoswine lead: Gyarados walls Talonflame (Brave Bird only 17-27% with Intimidate), immune to Garchomp EQ, Taunt shuts Spiritomb. Back: Gengar-Mega traps weakened targets with Shadow Tag; Corviknight provides Tailwind speed control, EQ immunity, and U-turn to safely pivot Gengar in. Handles all likely opponent leads.

Plan: Turn 1 Protect Gyarados (scout) + Ice Shard/Protect Mamoswine. Bring Gengar in via Corviknight U-turn or after a KO to trap with Shadow Tag. Watch for Calm Mind setup — Gengar Sludge Bomb SE or switch to defensive core. Klefki and Toxapex benched this game; consider for Game 2 if opponent adapts to physical lead.

decisions.rationale: Rock Slide (100-142%) and Waterfall (102-148%) both OHKO Talonflame; no Protect available. Switch to Rotom-Wash which walls Mamoswine (EQ immune, Ice Shard/Waterfall resisted) and resists Gyarados. Spiritomb Will-O-Wisp Mamoswine (85%) to halve its Attack; Rock Slide only does 18-26% to Spiritomb so it's safe. Preserves Talonflame for later Tailwind.

reflections.summary: Won because Rotom-Wash pressured Corviknight and Mega Gengar while Spiritomb's burn and Sucker Punch limited Mamoswine, allowing Talonflame to clean. The team-preview plan was only partially right: Rotom-Wash and Spiritomb fit, but Talonflame was fragile against Gyarados and Floette/Floettite was unused; not Mega Evolving was acceptable.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, lead or preserve Rotom-Wash as the primary Gyarados answer and avoid switching Talonflame into Gyarados; use Thunderbolt on Gyarados unless Protect is expected, and conserve Thunderbolt PP against double Protect.
reflections.notebook: Opponent brought Gengar-Mega, Corviknight, Mamoswine, Gyarados; benched Klefki and Toxapex. All four brought Protect, so expect Protect-heavy stalling and safe turns. Gengar Mega Evolves, likely Timid, and carries Thunderbolt. Gyarados has Intimidate and Sitrus; Rotom-Wash Thunderbolt is the best answer, though Protect can waste it. Mamoswine is Focus Sash/Thick Fat with Ice Shard, Rock Slide, Earthquake, and Protect; burn greatly reduces its physical threat, and Talonflame Flare Blitz can finish it when weakened. Corviknight is Leftovers/MirrorArmor and weak to Thunderbolt but can Protect. Future plan: favor Rotom-Wash + Spiritomb lead, keep Rotom healthy for Gyarados, avoid exposing Talonflame to Waterfall, and use Talonflame as a cleaner with Quick Guard for priority. Reevaluate bringing Floette; only commit Floettite if Rotom is compromised and a Gengar answer is needed.

reflections.summary: Lost because the four brought were poorly matched: Corviknight is 4x weak to Rotom-W Thunderbolt and spent turns 5-7 double-Protecting uselessly while Mamoswine was burned and chipped to sash-less range. Gengar-Mega accomplished nothing—used Protect turn 3, took damage off-screen, and entered at 32% only to immediately faint. The team played far too passively (repeated Protects) against an opponent running Protect-heavy stall + priority chip, allowing free burn and Thunderbolt damage with no offensive pressure in return.
reflections.adjustment: Drop Corviknight from the bring—it has no safe role when Rotom-W is guaranteed. Replace with a Pokémon that can threaten Rotom-W and break the opponent's Protect-stall pattern. Lead more aggressively: use Gengar-Mega's Shadow Tag to lock targets and deal damage immediately instead of Protecting. If keeping Gengar-Mega as the Mega, it must trap and eliminate Rotom-W or Spiritomb early; otherwise consider a different Mega holder that better handles the opponent's priority + stall core.
